models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light, benign pattern over the Aeolians this week — but the 3 Oct departure is well beyond any model's reach.
briefing.synopsis: Through the current forecast window the Aeolians sit under a slack, low-gradient pattern: winds start W/SW at 5-10 kt on 25 Sep, drop to near calm late afternoon, then settle into a light NE-to-N flow of roughly 5-10 kt on 26-27 Sep (ECMWF IFS 0.25°, 24 Sep 18Z, with ICON-2i 25 Sep 00Z and ECMWF AIFS 24 Sep 18Z in broad agreement). Seas stay small throughout — total wave 0.3 to 2.1 ft and swell 0.2 to 1.8 ft (MFWAM 24 Sep 12Z, cross-checked by ECMWF WAM 0.25° 24 Sep 18Z). The data run out at 23:00 on 1 October; the flotilla departs 3 October, so nothing here covers the trip dates. If this light-air regime held, the leg plan would be mostly motoring and gentle reaching, but eight days out that is a pattern impression, not a forecast.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: For the rehearsal night of 25 Sep the recommended berth is Portorosa Marina — enclosed, all-round shelter, and the choice does not matter in this air. Portorosa shows 1.6 kt from the NNW at 18:00 easing overnight, with wave around 0.9-1.0 ft (ECMWF IFS 0.25°, 24 Sep 18Z). Nothing in the payload would push the fleet to move. Note this is a dry run against live weather, not a berth forecast for the trip.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: 26 Sep looks like an early, easy start: Portorosa 2.6 kt from the ESE at 06:00 building to about 5-6 kt N by midday; Lipari 6.7 kt NE gusting 14.4; Filicudi the windiest at 10.7 kt NE gusting 22.7 (ECMWF IFS 0.25°, 24 Sep 18Z). Waves 1.0-1.6 ft across the group. A 06:00 departure window is clean in this pattern — but again, for the actual 3-4 October departure I have no data and will not guess.

cautions: Everything above is a rehearsal against current weather. The forecast horizon ends 1 Oct 23:00 — there is no model data for any trip date, and the pattern can change completely in eight days.
Models already disagree meaningfully at midday 25 Sep: Panarea 5.3-14.0 kt and Filicudi 6.7-13.2 kt across the model spread. Treat the 9-10 kt consensus figures at that hour as a range, not a number.

Gust figures at Stromboli and Filicudi reach 33.2 kt at 12:00 on 25 Sep against wind of only 7.0 and 9.9 kt. ECMWF IFS gusts are an interval maximum, so the gust factor is exaggerated in light air — but katabatic acceleration off Stromboli's cone is real and worth respect.
Marina del Gabbiano at Stromboli scores only 'workable' even in this calm: it is open from every direction and shelter there depends entirely on conditions staying light.
briefing.confidence_note: Model agreement is good inside the short range — mean wind shift run-to-run is 0.6-1.4 kt out to 120 h — but direction shift already averages 52° at 72-120 h, and the trip dates lie entirely beyond the 1 Oct forecast limit.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
